title: Fair terms give a shared word weight

captions.physics: Naming each person’s consent before promising
captions.energy: Matching requests to both people’s possibilities
captions.emotions: Feeling supported by a shared meaning

meaning: You can choose a promise through two honest replies and feel its weight when shared wording fits both people’s actual possibilities.
text: The weight of a shared promise depends partly on how it was chosen. The Lovers in the physical position of Vishuddha give each person room to name consent personally. Justice in energy supports an honest proportion between request and actual participation. The Hierophant in emotions gives support through shared meaning. An agreement can feel personally yours when it expresses a recognised value without requiring one reply regardless of individual circumstances. A familiar promise becomes warmer with both people present inside it.

For example, you discuss avoiding further heated argument through messages. One person wants to wait until meeting; the other needs acknowledgement that the question remains. **Shared meaning grows stronger through fair terms.** A brief phrase and a time for continuation can be agreed without making silence the only correct expression of respect. Chosen words become support because each knows what they promise and what they leave free. Consent can come from personal understanding.

The difficulty begins if a correct formula replaces a response to a new request. Someone is explaining how the present case differs while the rule is repeated. Clarifying specifics preserves seriousness. Trust in words can include questions and a willingness to hear two personal replies again, sustaining honest participation when circumstances have actually changed.
